easy.def: To make someone afraid.
examples: The loud noise scared me.
Do not scare the cat.
The ghost story scares him.

more.def: To make a person or animal feel afraid.
examples: The thunder scared the puppy.
Don't scare the birds away.
The movie scared the little kids.

easy.def: Afraid.
examples: The puppy is scared of thunder.
I felt scared in the dark.
She was scared of the big dog.

more.def: Feeling fear because you think something bad may happen.
examples: He felt scared when the lights went out.
The kitten was scared by the loud noise.
She was scared to jump into the deep end.

easy.def: Making you feel afraid.
examples: The dark cave was scary.
I told a scary story.
The thunder is scary.

more.def: Causing fear, so that you feel nervous or frightened.
examples: The old haunted house looked scary at night.
The roller coaster was scary but fun.
Some kids find big dogs scary until they get to know them.

easy.def: To throw or move things all over.
examples: We scatter seeds for the birds.
The wind scatters the leaves.
The birds scattered when the cat came.

more.def: To throw or spread things over a wide area, or to move apart quickly.
examples: The marbles scattered across the floor when the bag broke.
The crowd scattered when the rain began.
He scattered salt on the icy steps.

easy.def: A view of a place.
examples: The beach was a nice scene.
It was a pretty winter scene.
The painting shows a farm scene.

more.def: A view of a place and the things in it, as in a picture.
examples: The painting shows a quiet farm scene.
We looked at the snowy winter scene from the window.
A pretty scene of mountains and a lake hung on the wall.

easy.def: A part of a play or movie.
examples: The first scene was funny.
My scene is next.
She forgot her lines in the scene.

more.def: One part of a play, movie or book that happens in one place or time.
examples: In the first scene, the curtain rose on a forest.
The funniest scene in the movie was the food fight.
We rehearsed the last scene again.

easy.def: A list of times for things.
examples: The bus schedule is here.
Check the schedule.
Our schedule is busy.

more.def: A list that shows when things will happen.
examples: The bus schedule shows when the next bus comes.
Check the schedule to see when the game starts.
Our class has a busy schedule on Fridays.

easy.def: A place where children go to learn.
examples: I walk to school.
School starts at eight.
Our school is big.

more.def: A place where students go to learn from teachers.
examples: Our school has a library, a gym, and a garden.
The school bus picks us up at the corner.
She goes to school five days a week.

easy.def: Learning about the world by testing ideas.
examples: I like science class.
Science is fun.
We do science tests.

more.def: The study of how the world works, using careful tests and observation.
examples: We learned about volcanoes in science class.
Science helps us understand weather.
She wants to study science when she grows up.

easy.def: A person who studies how the world works.
examples: The scientist looked in a microscope.
Scientists study space.
I want to be a scientist.

more.def: A person who studies nature and the world through careful tests and observations.
examples: The scientist put the water under the microscope.
Scientists study volcanoes to learn how they work.
She became a scientist who studies whales.

easy.def: The number of points in a game.
examples: The score is two to one.
What is the score?
Our team has a high score.

more.def: The number of points a person or team has in a game.
examples: The score was tied at three.
What was the score of the game?
She got a perfect score on the test.

easy.def: To get a point.
examples: I scored a goal.
She scores in every game.
He scored a run.

more.def: To get a point or points in a game.
examples: She scored two goals in the soccer game.
He scored the winning run.
Our team scored in the last minute.

easy.def: To rub with your nails.
examples: I scratch my arm.
The cat scratched the chair.
The dog scratches its ear.

more.def: To rub or scrape something with fingernails or claws.
examples: The cat scratched the couch.
The dog scratched its ear.
I scratched the itchy bite.

easy.def: A thin mark or small cut.
examples: There is a scratch on the car.
I have a scratch on my arm.
The cat left a scratch.

more.def: A thin mark or shallow cut made by something sharp.
examples: There is a scratch on the car door.
The thorn left a scratch on my arm.
The cat left a scratch on the table.

easy.def: To yell in a loud, high voice.
examples: She screamed when she saw the spider.
The kids scream on the ride.
We screamed with joy.

more.def: To make a loud, high cry because you are scared, excited or hurt.
examples: The riders screamed with excitement on the roller coaster.
She screamed when a mouse ran by.
The baby screamed for a bottle.

easy.def: A loud, high cry.
examples: I heard a scream.
A scream came from the ride.
His scream was loud.

more.def: A loud, high cry of fear, pain or excitement.
examples: A scream came from the roller coaster.
We heard a scream from the haunted house.
She let out a scream of joy.

easy.def: The flat part of a TV or computer that shows pictures.
examples: I looked at the screen.
The TV screen is big.
The screen is bright.

more.def: The flat part of a television, phone or computer that shows pictures and words.
examples: The movie played on a huge screen.
Too much time in front of a screen can make your eyes tired.
The screen showed a picture of the moon.

easy.def: A net on a window that keeps bugs out.
examples: Close the screen door.
A bug is on the screen.
The screen has a hole.

more.def: A frame with a fine net in it that covers a window or door to keep out insects.
examples: The screen on the window kept the mosquitoes out.
Dad patched a hole in the porch screen.
A moth rested on the screen door.

easy.def: A thin metal pin with a twisty edge.
examples: Dad used a screw to hang the shelf.
The screw is loose.
I found a screw on the floor.

more.def: A small metal pin with a spiral edge that is twisted into wood or metal to hold things together.
examples: Dad drove a screw into the wall to hang the picture.
A loose screw made the chair wobble.
A box of screws sat on the workbench.

easy.def: To twist something on tight.
examples: Screw the lid on.
Dad screwed the shelf to the wall.
Screw in the light bulb.

more.def: To fasten something by twisting it, or by using a metal pin with a spiral edge.
examples: Screw the lid on tightly so the jam does not spill.
Dad screwed the hook into the beam.
She screwed the bulb into the lamp.

easy.def: The words that actors say in a play or movie.
examples: The actors read the script.
I forgot my lines in the script.
The script has the words.

more.def: The written words of a play, movie or show, telling the actors what to say and do.
examples: The actors learned their lines from the script.
She wrote a script for a puppet show.
The director gave everyone a copy of the script.
